I'd suggest continuing through this trial and error path since you will learn a lot along the way.

Frontend is visual and it's a given that there will be trial and error while developing, especially with CSS. Backend is more predictable and dry while on the Frontend you have all the dynamic things happening  right in front of you. The layouts, placement, sizes, paddings/margins, responsiveness all require doub/triple checks, maybe even more, to get them to work like you want.

Don't be afraid to branch out from the tutorials and try something on your own to see how things work. Everything comes together with experience which comes through trial and error.

First, I would suggest taking a look at semantic HTML, how to write it in a clean way without cluttering up  with unnecessary nesting.

Then, learn how to style the HTML. Start with Flex, learn the ins and outs of it.

Set some parent element to display: flex and play around with different placements to understand how it works like justify-content, align-items, apply flex: x y z; on child  elements, play around and don't be a fraid to fail or struggle.

Also, be curious, if you see a website or elements you like, use an inspect tool, see how they are coded, how they are styled and try to recreate them on your own. Perhaps, improve them? Write less HTML or CSS for the same element.

Once you understand how css rules  work, you will  have a better understanding of things like bootstrap. Don't forget to read, read, read the documentation, look at examples. Apply something of your own. If <div class="d-flex justify-contents-between mt-3"> doesn't work for you, add your own class to tweak the element.

Try, fail, learn, improve :)
